goals: Make Block Geometry Extensions geometries participate in Continuity connected-texture behavior when their canonical source or material-family semantics call for connection.
Preserve source-material identity and support applicable BGE-owned geometries consistently without duplicating BGE's canonical geometry ownership, material-family registry, or source-block mappings.
scope: Provide one centralized Fabric block-appearance bridge for eligible BGE-owned geometry without generating material- or geometry-specific CTM rules.
Consume BGE's typed runtime binding and canonical parent as the sole derived-to-material authority rather than inferring families from registry identifiers.
Project only explicitly equivalent canonical material state while keeping geometry form, orientation, waterlogging, and unknown properties out of the canonical appearance.
Apply a fail-closed geometry and visual eligibility policy that can broaden or tighten without per-material rules.
Preserve vanilla, non-BGE, Continuity, BGE, Matcha, and resource-pack behavior outside the bounded appearance bridge.

exclusions: Continuity remains the target CTM implementation; this project does not replace Continuity or implement a general CTM engine.

BGE retains ownership of geometry registration, geometry ownership, material-family relationships, and source-block mappings; this project must consume those canonical relationships rather than duplicate them or infer them from registry names.
Nibaru retains ownership of its material definitions and semantics.
This project does not modify BGE, Matcha, or unrelated resource-pack artwork during initialization.

Translucent Glass × BGE Compatibility remains a separate project responsible for translucent-glass and rendering compatibility issues that are not general CTM connectivity; this project does not absorb that scope.

dependencies.reason: Block Geometry Extensions owns the typed runtime binding, geometry roles, and canonical material relationships consumed directly by Canary 1; C70 is the first controlled compatibility baseline for this API seam.
Continuity is the optional target connected-texture consumer of Fabric block appearance; the bridge does not patch or bundle it.
The appearance and block-state method descriptors are compiled and controlled against Minecraft Java 26.2.
Fabric runtime loader and Mixin host declared by Canary 1.
Provides the Fabric block appearance and controlled GameTest APIs used by Canary 1; 0.156.0+26.2 is the exact validation baseline.
Owns the Vertical Slab and Step base classes targeted by the centralized appearance mixin; 2.0.7+26.2 is the exact controlled baseline.

state.milestone: Canary 1 implements the audited typed canonical-appearance bridge for full four-Layers and double Vertical Slabs, passes controlled state/eligibility GameTests and artifact checks, and remains runtime untested pending the manual Continuity matrix.

exceptions.reason: The appearance bridge is compiled against the Minecraft 26.2 block-state and Fabric appearance method descriptors and must remain on the controlled target release.
regression_evidence: Canary 1 compiles and its focused headless GameTests execute against Minecraft 26.2 and Fabric API 0.156.0+26.2.

current.summary: Projects eligible full-volume BGE Layer and Vertical Slab states onto typed canonical material appearances with explicit state mapping.
